Every country in the Southern Hemisphere.why: A textbook rule stated in the lead of Wikipedia's Southern Hemisphere article and wherever seasons are explained: meteorological summer, the calendar-month convention, is December to February south of the equator, in every country there.

Meteorological summer in Namibia falls f.why: People say it is summer from December to February south of the equator, and that Namibia lies in the south, so both premises are common talk. notes: Dev TBox contraction, paired with geography-replace-d005: removes the original rule 'Every country in the Southern Hemisphere has its meteorological summer from December to February' and puts nothing in its place. The own and propositional queries become unknown (strong Kleene); the negation question reads 'it is not the case that every country ...', denying the whole rule. The rule is about meteorological summer, the calendar-month convention, so tropical wet and dry seasons and astronomical dates do not bear on it. Derived: summer in Namibia, Mozambique and Madagascar (inheritance, 2 hops; the third an application). The removed rule is expected to be given up together with whatever supports it (such as northern winter months and reversed seasons), so a gold "I don't know" stands even where the months could be rebuilt. Same facts, checks and evidence as the revision. Near unrelated asks about the other hemisphere; delete is exempt from Rule 7.
